title: Occurrence, Preparation, and Properties of Phosphorus
lead: Phosphorus is prepared industrially from calcium phosphate, and the preparation of many of its compounds begins with its oxide P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>10</sub>. It forms two common oxides, P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>6</sub> and P<sub>4</sub>O<sub>10</sub>, and halides with the halogens, the most important of them the chlorides PCl<sub>3</sub> and PCl<sub>5</sub>.
objectives: Describe the properties, preparation, and uses of phosphorus
summary_html: Phosphorus (group 15) commonly exhibits oxidation states of 3− with active metals and of 3+ and 5+ with more electronegative nonmetals. The halogens and oxygen will oxidize phosphorus. The oxides are phosphorus(V) oxide, P4O10, and phosphorus(III) oxide, P4O6. The two common methods for preparing orthophosphoric acid, H3PO4, are either the reaction of a phosphate with sulfuric acid or the reaction of water with phosphorus(V) oxide. Orthophosphoric acid is a triprotic acid that forms three types of salts.

What volume of 0.200 M NaOH is necessary to neutralize the solution produced by dissolving 2.00 g of PCl3 is an excess of water? Note that when H3PO3 is titrated under these conditions, only one proton of the acid molecule reacts.

answer.hint: Water turns each PCl<sub>3</sub> into H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>3</sub> and three HCl; count the moles of acid that react with NaOH, one proton from each H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>3</sub> and one from each HCl.

exercises.prompt: How many tons of Ca<sub>3</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub> are necessary to prepare 5.0 tons of phosphorus if the yield is 90%?

answer.hint: Each Ca<sub>3</sub>(PO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>2</sub> holds two phosphorus atoms; find the mass of phosphate that holds 5.0 tons of phosphorus, then divide by the 90% yield.

exercises.prompt: Why does phosphorous acid form only two series of salts, even though the molecule contains three hydrogen atoms?

answer.solution: Suggested approach: draw the Lewis structure of phosphorous acid, H<sub>3</sub>PO<sub>3</sub>, and note which atom each hydrogen atom is bonded to. Recall which hydrogen atoms of an oxyacid ionize, and count how many of the three can be lost to a base; each one lost gives one series of salts.
